records.title: Rational 2^-240 enclosures of the nine Math-#223 c/c2 closed forms
records.layer_a_status: A1/A2: no Lean declaration states any enclosure; no axiom is involved. A3: not blocking. The evaluation path is exact integer/Fraction outward-rounded interval arithmetic with explicit series remainders and no binary floating point, and the enclosures rest on the cited DLMF 5.11(ii) remainder bound. A4: intervals transcribed as recorded, not loosened. A5: no test is recorded as failing at the final state; the scaffold failures and the cache defect are history (REVIEW.md:139-144; VALIDATION.md:6-11). The cone-omission and shrinkage tests are passing tests that assert a wrong variant is rejected, not failing controls. A6 (vacuity): the nine targets are explicit closed forms, so the claim is not vacuous. test_numerical_interval_shrink_mutant is a vacuous check. A7 (blocking): the ACCEPT of the published enclosures is review content of Math-#223. The tighter enclosures are a reviewer-side computation that the source calls a certificate, with scientific effect NONE. VALIDATION.md's test count (37) does not match the 38 methods in the files. No promotion. A8 (blocking): the enclosures are certified only by oracle.py, the directory's own reviewer-authored tool, which has not been independently reviewed or verified (REVIEW.md:24-25). It is described here from its code, not executed.
records.exact_boundary: The source's claim covers two things only. (1) Nine internal rational intervals, which the source says have width < 10^-45 (REVIEW.md:101; VALIDATION.md:15-16), for the displayed closed forms c1dim, c2dim, c3dim, corr1, corr2, corr3 and the three ratios of the reference Gaussian kernel (REVIEW.md:87-93), as computed by oracle.py under the DLMF 5.11(ii) remainder bound. RESULTS.json records only their outward-rounded 40-decimal displays, of width 10^-40, as independent_rational_interval. (2) Strict containment of those intervals in the nine PUBLISHED decimal pairs copied into oracle.py:15-24. Conditions the source names: the evaluator is reviewer-authored and not independently reviewed (REVIEW.md:24-25). Equality of the copied pairs with the upstream RESULTS.json, and authentication of the six source blobs, are left to a hosted verify.py run that local replay excludes (REVIEW.md:153-159; VALIDATION.md:27-30). Institutional human review and parent-kernel formalization are unsupplied (REVIEW.md:174-175). Excluded: identification with persistence-law coefficients; the jet/Isserlis derivation, finite part, cone comparison and candidate/elder asymptotics; any finite-L or SIDE24 c2 statement (REVIEW.md:16-20); the general correctness and portability of the source engine and its unused routines (REVIEW.md:110-111, 123-126); and the imported A_r = A~_r + O(r^3) relation (REVIEW.md:132-135). Nothing is proved here.
records.blocking_reason: A kernel proof of the enclosures needs formal rational interval bounds for pi (Machin with alternating atan tails), log (the atanh-type series with its tail bound), exp (Taylor tail with halving and squaring), integer n-th root brackets, and Gamma(1/6) and Gamma(5/6). The Gamma bounds rest on the positive-real Stirling remainder |log Gamma(y) - S(y)| <= |B42|/(42*41*y^41) at y = q + 40 (DLMF 5.11(ii)), which the directory imports by citation and does not prove. All nine closed forms must then be assembled with the stated widths. Whether these expressions are the Gaussian persistence coefficients is a separate open analytic question outside this record.
records.attempted: An independent integer/Fraction interval evaluator: Machin pi; 100-term series with rational tail bounds; exp by halving and repeated squaring; integer root brackets; Stirling log-Gamma with shift 40 through B40 and a B42 remainder. Also strict containment checks, a test suite (38 methods in the files; VALIDATION.md reports 37) including a cone-omission falsifier, and a typed-cache repair.
records.resumption_cost: Moderate to high for a kernel reproduction of the nine enclosures at the stated width. It needs formal elementary series bounds, the DLMF 5.11(ii) Stirling remainder through B40/B42 (not available as a checked lemma), and kernel evaluation of 2^-240-scale rationals. A coarser kernel check of containment in the published pairs (width about 10^-14) would still need a formal Gamma enclosure. High for any identification with persistence coefficients. Dormant until deliberately reopened.

records.classification_reason: Part review, part new computation. Review content: REVIEW.md:9-14 ACCEPTs the nine published enclosures of Math-#223 at 59a06b65 (SOURCE_BINDINGS.json:3-29 binds the six frontiers/c2_exact_20261001 files). Section 3 (REVIEW.md:106-126) inspects the branches the source engine reaches. Section 4 (REVIEW.md:128-135) states that the successor NOTE closes the notation/scope defect OA-223-A-01. New content: the reviewer-written Fraction evaluator oracle.py forms nine outward-rounded 2^-240 rational enclosures of the supplied closed forms (REVIEW.md:87-93), which the source says have width < 10^-45 (REVIEW.md:101-104; VALIDATION.md:15-16). RESULTS.json records their outward 40-decimal displays as independent_rational_interval. For example, RESULTS.json:10-19 gives c in d = 1 as an interval of width 10^-40 against the published 0.1101103789590410-0.1101103789590625. REVIEW.md:103 calls this 'a new independent numerical certificate of those displayed expressions'. Enclosures this much tighter than any the reviewed object states are bounds of the record's own, so the record is a standalone claim for those enclosures. Strict containment in the published pairs is the review part. README.md:3-4 and REVIEW.md:16-20 disclaim any persistence theorem or coefficient identification.

source_statements.text:
Let A=Gamma(1/6)/12^(1/6), B=Gamma(5/6)12^(1/6), s=sqrt6. Then the supplied
expressions are

 c1dim=A/(6pi^(3/2)),       c2dim=A/(9pi^(3/2)),
 c3dim=(29/72-s/12)A/pi^(5/2),
 corr1=(3/4)B/pi^(3/2),     corr2=(13/18)B/pi^(3/2),
 corr3=(5/48)(33-7s)B/pi^(5/2).

Each resulting rational interval has width<10^-45. The program verifies strict
containment inside each original published decimal pair using Fractions. This
is a new independent numerical certificate of those displayed expressions,
not a comparison of a few floating digits or an extrapolation from a test grid.

records.source_hypotheses: The nine supplied closed forms for the reference Gaussian kernel in dimensions 1, 2, 3 (REVIEW.md:87-93), with A = Gamma(1/6)/12^(1/6), B = Gamma(5/6) 12^(1/6) and s = sqrt 6: the leading c, the correction c2, and c2/c. The ratios need strictly positive leading denominators, which REVIEW.md:97-98 states. The Gamma enclosure uses the positive-real Stirling remainder |log Gamma(y) - S(y)| <= |B42|/(42*41*y^41) at y = q + 40 (REVIEW.md:68-82). The strict-containment part also presupposes that the nine PUBLISHED pairs copied into oracle.py:15-24 equal the source RESULTS.json (REVIEW.md:156-159). The record neither assumes nor asserts that these expressions equal persistence coefficients (REVIEW.md:16-20).
records.source_dependencies: NIST DLMF 5.11(ii), the positive-real Stirling remainder for expansion 5.11.1 (REVIEW.md:74-80; README.md:26-27). The Machin identity for pi, the alternating atan series, log and exp power-series tail bounds and integer n-th root brackets, as written in REVIEW.md:39-64. The supplied closed forms and published decimal intervals of frontiers/c2_exact_20261001 (RESULTS.json, NOTE.md) at Math-#223 head 59a06b65 (SOURCE_BINDINGS.json).

records.finite_checks: oracle.py evaluates all nine closed forms in integer/Fraction interval arithmetic. It rounds outward to multiples of 2^-240, takes products and divisions over all endpoint corners and rejects zero-containing divisors (REVIEW.md:29-37; oracle.py:34-45). results() checks with Fractions that each internal interval lies strictly inside its published pair (oracle.py:159-164). No code checks the stated width < 10^-45; test_nine_published_enclosures asserts only width < 10^-40 (test_oracle.py:16-19). test_oracle.py has 26 test methods and test_bindings.py has 12, 38 in all. VALIDATION.md:7-13 records 26 + 11 = 37 passing, so its count does not match the files at this commit. The tests cover recurrence/reflection and integer Gamma identities, coefficient atoms, ratio formulas, radical brackets, all-corner arithmetic, signed outward rounding, a cone-omission falsifier (test_negative_cone_term_load_bearing), a typed-cache regression, and real local Git fixtures for source identity (REVIEW.md:139-151). The 'false endpoint shrinkage' test (test_numerical_interval_shrink_mutant, test_oracle.py:100-104) is tautological: an interval's upper endpoint is never below its midpoint minus 10^-30, so the test cannot fail. verify.py --local-only excludes historical source authentication (REVIEW.md:153-158; VALIDATION.md:27-30). None of this was re-run here.
records.floating_point: NONE: oracle.py uses Python ints and fractions.Fraction, with math.comb, factorial and isqrt applied to integers only. It rounds outward to 2^-240 with integer floor/ceiling (oracle.py:30-37) and builds the 40-decimal display from integers (oracle.py:154-157). RESULTS.json records binary_float_used false. test_oracle.py uses Fraction; the float 0.5 appears there (lines 85 and 91) only as an input that must be rejected. verify.py and test_bindings.py do Git, hashing and JSON bookkeeping only, with no numerical arithmetic bearing on a bound.

problems_fixed.issue: REVIEW_OF is wrong. Besides accepting the published enclosures, the record certifies its own enclosures: oracle.py produces nine outward-rounded 2^-240 rational intervals of width < 10^-45 (REVIEW.md:101-104; VALIDATION.md:15-16), stored as independent_rational_interval in RESULTS.json. Example: RESULTS.json:10-19 encloses c in d = 1 to 40 decimals, while the published pair has width about 2e-14. REVIEW.md:103 calls this 'a new independent numerical certificate of those displayed expressions'. These bounds are about 26 orders of magnitude tighter than anything the reviewed object claims, so they are a certificate of something the reviewed object did not claim, which makes the record STANDALONE_CLAIM.
All of these are 'n/a', but a standalone record needs them. They are filled in the corrected record.

source_statements.text:
lim_{R -> oo} limsup_{r -> 0} r^-3 E_{Q_r^W} #{ ordered pairs (X, X') of distinct window points :
                                                     not both |X - o| <= R r and |X' - o| <= R r } = 0.       (Res)

Therefore `limsup_r r^-3 M_R = 2 a_2 - 2 a_2^R` (a full limit, by 1 and 2), which tends to `0` as `R -> oo` by 3. That is
(Res). ∎

records.layer_a_status: A3: the numerical intervals and the C_BOUNDS, K_BOUNDS, TB_EXACT and T2_IDENTITY checks are decimal or binary floating-point evaluations, and are not admitted as certification of any bound. records.exact_boundary: The exact claims are: (i) the README §4 / RESULTS.json intervals are stated to enclose J_hat, T_1, T_2, T_b and the table constants J_cusp, c, kappa c, B_sign, C_*, G_max, G_2, B_2 and singleton, for k in {1/2,1,2} and b in {0,1}; as a by-product, pi, log 2, erf(1/2) and D are stated to be enclosed to more than 40 digits (README.md:39). These quantities are defined by formulas that pass through Math-#178's unreviewed planar reduction. Every enclosure also assumes that the decimal module's exp and sqrt are correctly rounded (README.md:43-45). (ii) Identities (a)-(c) of README §3, with the reduced forms of B_sign (:108) and of C_2 and c(k) (:121). (iii) Consequence 1 (:126-128): the table depends only on J_hat=I_11 and T_1=12 I_11-11 I_9, and the family obeys (1+p) I_p - p I_(p-2) = 72 k^2 (I_(p+6) - I_(p+4)). (iv) Consequence 2: 66451/11128 < c(k) < 199353/2782 for every k>0 at [Q] (13) scope, with both ends stated to be sharp as limits. (v) Consequence 3: explicit bounds for all k on J_hat, I_9, B_sign, c and C_*. The source excludes finite-r statements, rates in r, C8 constants, the near-mass identity (N), the remote singleton population (README.md:231), d>2, and other kernels or frames. It leaves the formal asymptotic series (:168-172) with uncertified remainders. Floating-point interval output is not admitted as a bound. Nothing is proved by this record.
records.blocking_reason: Identities (a)-(c) and Consequences 1-3 are hand calculus (substitution, integration by parts, Taylor bounds with Gaussian moments) with no kernel formalization. The planar reduction that defines the enclosed numbers (p_b(0)/z_0 and the one-dimensional cusp integrals of Math-#178 §1) is consumed but unreviewed. Enclosing the transcendental integrals would need exact rational interval quadrature with explicit Taylor remainders, or a formal proof, in place of decimal floating point with library-rounded exp and sqrt.

It uses Machin's formula for pi and series for log 2 and erf(1/2), cross-checks by nesting and truncation-nesting, runs eleven mutants, and applies a v1.3 rigor repair to Decimal negation (README.md:41-93, :250-260).
records.resumption_cost: Moderate for identities (b) and (c) and for Consequences 1 and 2.    cancellation is one of expectations). This does not improve Theorem R: the near remainder is dominated by

source_statements.text:
Let mu be a probability measure, X a measurable real random variable, and
assume X^2, X^4 and X^6 are integrable. Write

    s = E[X^2], m4 = E[X^4], m6 = E[X^6],
    g = m4 - s^2, Delta = m6 - m4^2/s.

Choose a,b != 0 with a^2 != b^2, and p,q>0 such that

    mu{X=a} >= p, mu{X=b} >= q, p+q <= 1.

T(t) >= T_floor
       := min(delta0,(delta0+9*s0*g0)/4) > 0.         (5.4)

source_statements.text:
Take distinct squared radii s,t > 0 and lower masses p,r > 0 such that

    P(X^2=s) >= p, P(X^2=t) >= r.

Thus p+r <= 1. The masses aggregate both signs; no symmetry or independence is
assumed. Put H(u,v)=uv/(u+v) for nonnegative u,v with positive sum, and

    ell = p*s + r*t,
    g = H(p,r)*(s-t)^2,
    d = H(p*s,r*t)*(s-t)^2.

All three numbers are strictly positive. The conclusion is

    m2 >= ell, G >= g, Delta >= d.                         (1)

Then

    0 < D_lower <= D(q) <= D_upper,
    0 < N_lower/D_upper <= S(q),
    0 < T_lower <= T(q).                                 (5)

source_statements.text:
Lemma D2 (line 116) is `|det H| <= ||H e|| K^(d-1)`. With `||H_i e_x|| <= L r/2`
it gives

    |det H_i| <= (L r / 2) K^(d-1) <= (r / 2) K^d,          i in {M, S},

using `L <= K` from §1.1 (line 28), where `L` is the Hessian Lipschitz
constant on the chart and `K` dominates `1 + ||f||_(C^6)`. `L` is not a fixed
constant and cannot be absorbed into `C`: for `0 < r <= 1` and `L = K = A`,
the matrix `H = diag(r A/2, A, ..., A)` has operator norm `A` and exactly the
permitted short column, but `|det H| / (r K^(d-1)) = A/2` is unbounded in `A`.
The display as printed therefore omits the factor `L` (equivalently, after
`L <= K`, one power of `K`): the discrepancy is unbounded, not a constant. The
corrected display is the one above.

which is what the corrected endpoint bounds give: `W_r = F_d(H_M) F_(d-1)(H_S)
<= |det H_M| |det H_S| <= (r^2/4) K^(2d)` (with equality on the typed support
and `W_r = 0` off it) and `|det H_X| <= K^d`. The faulty intermediate display
would have given the *smaller* power `K^(3d-2)`, which the source never used.
After the single division by [LP] (5.5), `Z_r >= z_* r^2`, the paragraph's
conclusion `W_r |det H_X| / Z_r <= C K^(3d)` on the whole strip `|v| <= s^(1/8)`
stands as written, and §6.5 (line 528) consumes exactly that `K^(3d)` bound.

source_statements.text:
Under these hypotheses:

    |f_x + (r^2/8) f_xxx|              <= M r^4 / 384,             (M1)
    |f_xx + (r^2/24) f_xxxx|           <= M r^4 / 1920,            (M2)
    |f_xxx - 12 k|                    <= (3/80) M r^2,           (M3)
    |f(0)-b + (k/2) r^3|              <= (121/15360) M r^4,       (M4)
    |f_x/r^2 + 3 k/2|                 <= (7/960) M r^2,          (M5)
    |f_z + (r^2/8) f_xxz|             <= M r^4 / 384,             (M6)
    |f_xz + (r^2/24) f_xxxz|          <= M r^4 / 1920.            (M7)

These constants are explicit sufficient bounds; no optimality is claimed.

For x=r u,z=r v, Taylor gives the corrected leading longitudinal row

    f_x(ru,rv)/r^2
      = 6k (u^2-1/4)
        + f_xxz(0) u v
        + (1/2) f_xzz(0) v^2
        + O(r),

uniformly on a fixed compact scaled annulus when the required fourth/fifth derivatives are uniformly bounded.

The pin-preserving perturbation `(x^2-r^2/4)^2` has zero value and gradient at both pins. Its contribution to `f_x(ru,0)/r^2` is

    4 r u(u^2-1/4).

At u=2 this equals 30r. Thus the S1 error cannot generally be strengthened from O(r) to O(r^2) merely by assuming C6 bounds. This identifies the first residual order without claiming any conditional Gaussian covariance or density estimate.

source_statements.text:
For all sufficiently small ell (depending on a,b,r0), the whole band satisfies
`r<=min(k,r0)` and `k<=1`. Substitution of (2.2), including `dr`, gives exactly

    nu_[a,b](ell)
      = ell^(1/2)/10 * integral_a^b J_ell(y) y^(-3/2) dy.              (2.3)

For ell sufficiently small that the whole support is inside `0<r<=r0` and
`k<=1/2`, theta=1 on the support. It suffices to take
`ell <= min(2^(-16), r0^(10/3))`, with `0<r0<=1`. Put
`t=ell^(3/2)/r^5`; then `k^3/r=t^2` and

    integral r^(-2) A_rej(r,ell/r^3) dr
      = integral ell^2 r^(-6) h(ell^(3/2)/r^5) dr
      = ell^(1/2)/5 * integral_1^2 (t-1)^4(2-t)^4 dt
      = ell^(1/2)/3150.                                           (3.3)

Split (4.1) into those two tails and [a,b], divide by ell^(1/2), first let
ell tend to zero, then exhaust the interval. The compact part is O(ell^(1/4))
after division, and (4.2) controls the tails. Hence `R(ell)=o(ell^(1/2))`.

source_statements.text:
Work on one probability space with N a nonnegative integer-valued count, K>=1,
a measurable event E, a small scale rho>0 and 0<Xi<=C0. Fix a>=0, 0<p<m and an
integer m>=2. Put theta=1-p/m. Assume only

    E[(N)_m] <= B_m rho,
    E[K^t 1_E] <= A_t rho Xi   for t=0 and t=a/theta.       (L-input)

Constants are independent of rho and Xi in the stated parameter range. Then

    E[K^a N^p 1_E]
       <= [m^m(A_0 C0+B_m)]^(p/m) A_(a/theta)^theta
          rho Xi^theta.                                  (L)

supplies the factorial bound. Consequently

    E[K^a N^p 1_E] <= C r^3 Xi^(1-p/m),
    E[K^a N_R^p 1_S] <= C r^3 Xi^(1-p/m).                 (4)

Fix an integer m>=2 and real 0<p<m. In the abstract d=3,q=1 case, let
r_n=2^(-mn), K=1. An ordinary atom has mass r_n^3, N_R=N=2,h_2=2; a rare atom has
mass r_n^7,N_R=N=2^(4n),h_2=r_n; the remaining mass has count0. Set h_1=r_n/2.
The probabilities sum to less than1 for n>=1.

For every eta in [0,1], E={N_R>0,h_2<=eta} is empty if eta<r_n and is the rare
atom otherwise. Thus E[K^t;E]<=r_n^3(eta+r_n)^4 for every t>=0. Also

    E[(N)_m] <= E[N^m] = (2^m+1)r_n^3.

At eta=r_n,

    E[N^p;E] = r_n^7 2^(4np)
              = r_n^3 r_n^[4(1-p/m)],
    Xi = (2r_n)^4.                                     (5)

The ratio to r_n^3 Xi^(1-p/m) is the nonzero constant16^[-(1-p/m)]. For any
larger Xi exponent, the ratio is unbounded as n increases. This proves sharpness
of 1-p/m from the listed single-order inputs. It is NOT a lower bound for the
actual Gaussian field. The next ordinary moment obeys

||nu_(r,s)-nu_(r,s)^keep||_variation
      = r^-3 E[(N_R)_s 1_S] <= C Xi^(1-s/m), m>s,m>=2.   (6)

       <= H_a exp[(beta+3-c y/2)u].                     (1)

        <= A_a + H_a exp[-c u y0/4] <= A_a+H_a=:M_a.    (EC)

fixed theta with 0<theta<=B/d set integer s(r)=floor(theta Lambda(r)), once it is

source_statements.text:
**Theorem LT.** Conditional on the quoted interfaces, for every fixed a>=0 and
s>0 there are C<infinity and r_*>0 such that throughout the fixed parameter set,

    E_(P_r)[K^a N^s 1_E]
       <= C r^3 Xi Lambda(r)^(d s),                   (LT)
    E_(P_r)[K^a N_R^s 1_S]
       <= C r^3 Xi Lambda(r)^(d s).                   (LT-local)

For each fixed integer s>=1, (N_R)_s<=N_R^s. Therefore deleting configurations in
S from the r^-3-rescaled positive ordered-s-tuple intensity changes its total
variation mass by at most C Xi Lambda^(ds), with the same K^a-weighted upper bound
for tuple observables bounded by K^a. The convention is total mass for a positive
measure, not half the L1 norm of probabilities. This concerns only the deleted
sector. There is no assertion of a full point-process limit, location density,
normalized factorial Palm law, local nonempty lower bound or elder selection.

Hence Lambda(r_j)/4<=v_j<=Lambda(r_j), and (7) lies between
4^(-ds)Lambda(r_j)^(ds)/16 and Lambda(r_j)^(ds)/16. It is not
O(1) and not o(Lambda(r_j)^(ds)). The same model works for each fixed s>0.

source_statements.text:
theorem p02_lm009_moment40_tail_finite
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (R : Ω → ℝ)
    (r ε M : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hRi : Integrable (fun x => R x ^ 40) μ)
    (hMbound : (∫ x, R x ^ 40 ∂μ) ≤ M) :
    (μ (badJetEvent R r ε)).toReal ≤ (M / ε ^ 8) * r ^ 8 := by

theorem p02_lm009_moment40_family_r3_interval
    (μ : ℝ → Measure Ω)
    (W R : ℝ → Ω → ℝ) (r0 ε M cW cZ : ℝ)
    (hr0 : 0 < r0 ∧ r0 ≤ 1) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hcW : 0 ≤ cW) (hcZ : 0 < cZ)
    (hdata : ∀ r, 0 < r → r ≤ r0 →
      IsProbabilityMeasure (μ r) ∧
      MemLp (W r) 2 (μ r) ∧ (0 ≤ᵐ[μ r] W r) ∧ Measurable (R r) ∧
      Integrable (fun x => R r x ^ 40) (μ r) ∧
      (∫ x, R r x ^ 40 ∂(μ r)) ≤ M ∧
      (∫ x, W r x ^ 2 ∂(μ r)) ≤ cW * r ^ 4 ∧
      cZ * r ^ 2 ≤ ∫ x, W r x ∂(μ r)) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ r, 0 < r → r ≤ r0 →
      IsProbabilityMeasure (weightedLaw (μ r) (W r)) ∧
      (weightedLaw (μ r) (W r) (badJetEvent (R r) r ε)).toReal ≤ C * r ^ 3 := by

source_statements.text:
gives, for the crest-to-trough amplitude `H` (a maximum to the following minimum) under the Palm distribution of maxima,

    f_H(h) ~ C h^{−1/3},     P(H ≤ h) ~ (3/2) C h^{2/3}     (h ↓ 0),
    C = Γ(7/6) · 72^{−1/6} (2π)^{−1/2} · (λ₆ − λ₄²/λ₂)^{2/3} / λ₄,

i.e. `C = 0.199718…` for the covariance `e^{−t²/2}` (`λ₂ = 1`, `λ₄ = 3`, `λ₆ = 15`).

It is then integrated over separations `t ≤ 1.5`. `h^{1/3}f(h)/(Cν_max)` equals `1.0048, 0.9971, 0.9984, 0.99941, 0.99982,
0.999951, 0.999989, 0.9999983, 1.0000003` at `h = 10⁻², …, 10⁻¹⁰`. The deviation shrinks by a factor of about `3.3–4.4`
per decade, i.e. roughly as `h^{0.57}`, consistent with a relative correction of order `h^{7/12}` (the cusp scale).
This checks the constant's arithmetic through the exact two-point Rice formula. It is not an independent proof of the
law, since intermediate extrema are not excluded, which affects only the regular part.

source_statements.text:
**Application.** There is a common Gaussian coupling X_r,Y of the actual
six-coordinate endpoint law under Q_r and its contact law such that, for
every fixed finite p>=1,

    ||X_r-Y||_Lp <= C_p r,    sup_r E||X_r||^p < infinity.       (A)

Here `Y=(-1,1,-a/2,a/2,Q,Q)` has the conditional law from [E], not an arbitrary
vector on that plane. With the physical typed weight W_r, define
`Z_r=E_Qr W_r`, `z_r=Z_r/r²` and `z0=E[(Q_-)²]`. Then

    z0>0,    E|T_r(X_r)-T_0(Y)| <= C r,
    |z_r-z0| <= C r,    z_r >= z0/2,                           (B)
    d_BL(nu_r,nu0) <= C_BL r,
    nu_r{c_+>=0} <= C_sign r².                                (C)

**Result.** Under exactly these hypotheses, the conditional means and
covariances of the six adjusted endpoint variables extend continuously to
r = 0, with limiting law

    (-1, 1, -a/2, a/2, Q_L, Q_L),

where (a,Q_L) is the conditional law of (f_xxy(0), f_yy(0)) given
J = (b,0,0,0,0,2). The six-dimensional limiting covariance is allowed to be
singular. All its conditional eighth moments are uniformly bounded for
sufficiently small r. Consequently the exact typed endpoint weight has
E[W_r²] ≤ C r⁴, and W_r/r² is uniformly integrable. The constants and the
sufficiently small radius are qualitative, not numerical certificates.

source_statements.text:
Set R=min(Rbar,lambda/(2 Lg)) when Lg>0, and R=Rbar if Lg=0.
For every r in [0,R], G_r is positive definite and the canonical conditional
law of V_r given P_r=d_r admits a joint Gaussian coupling X_r,X_0 with

 e_r^2=E||X_r-X_0||^2 <= K^2 r^2.                         (3)

The limiting A_- is the deterministic value -1. Any coupling to that limit
has mean-square error at least (15), of order r. Hence no coupling with
RMS error O(r) is possible in this example; its RMS error is bounded below by a positive multiple of sqrt(r).

source_statements.text:
**Theorem T1.** Let d>=1 be an integer and A,B arbitrary real numbers. On the
closed simplex Delta_d={x_i>=0, sum_i x_i=1}, define

    F(x) = A sum_i x_i^2 + B sum_i x_i^3.

Then

    min_Delta F = min_{1<=m<=d} (A/m + B/m^2),
    max_Delta F = max_{1<=m<=d} (A/m + B/m^2).                         (2)

**Corollary T2.** Under these input conditions, put

    v_m = 6a^3 + 9ab/m + (c-b^2/a)/m^2,     1<=m<=d.

Then min over unit u of tau(u)^2 is min_m v_m, and max is max_m v_m.

Derivative covariances are the spectral moments: the gradient covariance is aI, Var(t_u)=E[Y^6], and Cov(t_u,G_i) is minus E[Y^3 xi_i] for Y=sum_i u_i xi_i (:104-110). source_statements.text:
**Proposition P1.** For every unit direction in every finite dimension,

    tau_u^2 = Delta sum_i t_i^3
            + 9 m2 V2 sum_{i!=j} t_i^2 t_j
            + 36 m2^3 sum_{i<j<k} t_i t_j t_k.          (1)

**Corollary P2.** Let

    c_low = min{Delta, 3 m2 V2, 6 m2^3},
    c_high = max{Delta, 3 m2 V2, 6 m2^3}.

Then for EVERY finite d>=1 and every unit u,

    c_low <= tau_u^2 <= c_high,                         (3)
    tau_u^2 >= Delta/d^2.                               (4)

Do not use Delta alone as a dimension-free lower bound: for the symmetric
law with total mass 99/100 on {-1,1} and 1/100 on {-10,10}, the equal two-support
direction has variance strictly below its axis value Delta. This is a control,
not a claim that that discrete law is P's spectrum.

records.source_hypotheses: tau_u^2=Var(partial_u^3 f(0) | grad f(0)=0) for |u|=1, conditioning on the full gradient only, for jointly Gaussian field derivatives with a product spectral representation. X_1,...,X_d are independent copies of a symmetric real X with finite sixth moment and m2=E X^2>0. m4 and m6 are raw moments, Delta=m6-m4^2/m2, V2=m4-m2^2 and t_i=u_i^2 (NOTE.md:24-44). Application: P's variance-one covariance at a fixed L>0, with one-coordinate weights proportional to exp(-2 pi^2 n^2/L^2) at X=2 pi n/L (NOTE.md:111-118). The control (NOTE.md:106-109) uses the stated discrete symmetric law.

source_statements.text:
The printed event, "separation at least `η`", also contains pairs with separation greater than `δ_*`. Those pairs are estimated by (15) at the fixed separation `δ_*`, so their ordered expectation is `O((k r^3)^2)`. The repaired probability is

`P(separation at least η) ≤ E[T_{r,j,2}(η)]/2 + O((k r^3)^2)`.

On the compact mark set, `(k r^3)^2 / (k r^3) = k r^3` tends to 0 with `r`, uniformly for `k∈[k_-, k_+]`. For small `r_*` the second summand is absorbed, and the probability is at most `C k r^3`. The absorption uses the fixed-separation theorem at separation `δ_*`. It does not extend (15) down to `η=0`.

The fixed-`η` statement (15)–(16) remains the outer boundary for separations bounded below independently of `r`. Its probability `O(r^6)` is the bound in that regime. The divided-difference argument adds a uniform majorant `O(k r^3)` down to separation zero inside `D_ρ`. Uniformity is the gain. Sharpness is not claimed.

Then the cutoff-restricted moment is infinite, given the asserted positivity and continuity near y=y' of the full weighted kernel at separated sites, because the double integral of |y-y'|^(-beta) over I_r^2 diverges. The source states the conclusion for every cutoff whose retained pair set has positive measure. When that set lies in delta<eta_0, for example when diam E < eta_0 or for a collision-chart cutoff delta<=delta_0<eta_0, its argument as written does not apply, and kernel positivity at those distances is not argued. A cutoff larger than diam E gives zero. (N2) The comparison (M20) holds for every beta>=2/3 and q>=0, an elementary consequence of 0<Delta<ell_r=kr^3 and delta<=D_T. source_statements.text:
- **N1 (`β ≥ 1` at separated positions).** Consider a distance cutoff whose retained pair set in `E × E` has positive
  measure; this holds for every sufficiently small fixed cutoff when `E` has positive volume. At separated sites
  (`δ ≥ η_0`), the full weighted kernel is positive and continuous near the diagonal `y = y'`. That kernel is the
  joint height density given zero gradients, times `E[W_r F_i(H_x) F_j(H_{x'}) | …]` with the actual endpoint weight
  and witness determinants. Positivity comes from the distinct-jet support with the correct endpoint Hessian types and
  nonzero witness determinants; a positive Gaussian height density alone would not control a weight that could vanish
  on equal heights. Hence `∫∫_{I_r²}|y−y'|^{−β}(…) = ∞` for `β ≥ 1`, and every such cutoff moment is infinite. (A
  cutoff larger than `diam E` retains no pairs and gives zero.) This extends the note's deliberately weaker "need not
  regularize" remark; it is not a defect in Theorem M, and it gives a second route to the `β ≥ 1` part of (M20).

- **N2.** (M20) in fact covers every `β ≥ 2/3` and every `q ≥ 0`. For `2/3 ≤ β < 1` the positive diagonal (M7)
  already gives this.

records.source_hypotheses: The fixed-r setting of the reviewed PROOF.md (PROOF.md:11-35). The field is the variance-one periodized Gaussian field on a fixed torus of side L in fixed d>=2, with original pins M and S at heights b and b-kr^3 and zero gradients. Marks are compact, with k bounded away from zero, and all frames are allowed. The setting keeps the full weight W_r and normalizer Z_r, with Q_r^W=(W_r/Z_r)Q_r, a fixed positive-volume Borel E in D_rho, the window I_r, and the moment (M1) with weight delta^(-q) Delta^(-beta). N1 assumes: beta>=1; r fixed and sufficiently small; and a distance cutoff whose retained pair set in E x E has positive measure (true for every sufficiently small fixed cutoff when E has positive volume). Its argument is made at separated sites delta>=eta_0, where eta_0<=rho/2 is the near-diagonal chart radius of PROOF.md:132. So it needs the retained set to contain a positive-measure set of such separated pairs, which positive volume of E does not imply. It also uses positivity and continuity near the diagonal y=y' of the full weighted kernel: the joint height density given zero gradients times E[W_r F_i(H_x) F_j(H_x') | ...]. This is attributed to the distinct-jet support with the correct endpoint Hessian types and nonzero witness determinants. N2 assumes q>=0 and beta>=2/3, using (M7) for 2/3<=beta<1.

source_statements.text:
- **N1 (the conditioned law: closed by combination).** §8 says Theorem S "does not settle conditioned SARD-G". The
  perturbation (N8) is supported in an arbitrarily small neighbourhood `O` of a *regular* point of the unstable half.
  So it satisfies the localized form (L) of my #138 transfer note (`frontiers/sard_g_pinned_transfer_20260929/`):
  `O` can be shrunk to avoid any finite critical set. The note's Theorem P then gives the Theorem S conclusion for
  every law pinned in value and gradient at finitely many points with smooth mean **that satisfies Theorem P's
  hypothesis `Q(Ω_gen) = 1`**. Arbitrary pinned values can violate it, for example by forcing equal critical values.
  For R0's `Q_r` (distinct pin sites, gap `k > 0`, within the parent's validity regime) the accepted D1 parent §8
  supplies it, and `Q_r^W` follows by absolute continuity with respect to `Q_r`. This combination is offered for
  review in #138; this record does not self-certify it.

- **N3.** The volume bound (N12), `O(√ε)`, is valid and suffices for the union bound `O(√δ)`. It is not sharp: in
  `x = (a+c)/2`, `y = (a−c)/2` one has `ac − b² = x² − y² − b²`, and for each bounded `x` the set of admissible

Strictly, the bridge rests on the hand reduction in the docstring at 64-70, which I re-derived and found correct: 72^(-1/6) 6^(2/3) = 2^(1/6) 3^(1/3) = sqrt6 12^(-1/6); 3^(1/3) 6^(1/3) = 2^(1/3) 3^(2/3) = 12 sqrt3 12^(-5/6); Q = 1620 and 1620/2160 = 3/4; the results are (1/6) pi^(-3/2) and 9 pi^(-3/2). The float comparison should be described as a smoke test, not a certification.

The atanh remainder is computed in undirected binary64 with libm pow (m**55) and a safety factor of 2. This contradicts the ia.py 1-5 docstring claim that no libm transcendental is trusted. It is still sound for every reachable input. log_pt's reduction (60-65) gives |u| <= 0.1716, so the true tail is <= about 3e-44, far below the one-ulp widening of s (about 1e-17), and the underflow cases are absorbed by the minimum-subnormal step of nextafter in _with_err (20-22). An exact Fraction bound would remove the dependence on pow.

The exp Horner error bound is a hand-derived a priori bound, and err is evaluated in round-to-nearest. I checked it: coefficient error gamma_18 plus Horner error gamma_36 sum|c_i||z|^i gives 54u e^|z| (1+O(u)). The code's 56u(1+1e-12) + 1e-19 times 2.12 >= e^0.75 covers that, and the roughly 3u relative rounding in computing err is absorbed by the 2u slack. The truncation term is 0.75^19/19! e^|z|, about 3.5e-20 e^|z|. Sound, but resting on that hand analysis rather than on directed evaluation.

from_frac assumes float(q) is within one ulp of q, and it does not check that q <= up(f) or dn(f) <= q. This holds because CPython's int/int true division, used by Fraction to float, is correctly rounded. A check such as Fr(up(f)) >= q would make the routine verify itself.

The publication margin MARGIN*abs(iv) is computed undirected. It is not load-bearing: rounding is monotone, so fl(iv0 - x) <= iv0 and fl(iv1 + x) >= iv1 for x >= 0, and outward dn/up plus ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING follow (153). The margin only adds width.

The basic-operation soundness relies on platform facts that cannot be checked by reading the code: IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest with no x87 double rounding (true on standard x86-64/SSE2 or ARM64 CPython), a correctly rounded C sqrt, and Python 3.9 or later for math.nextafter.

It computes the error bound with gauss.error_bound (gauss.py 124-127). It takes interval nodes and weights from gauss.rule/panel (68-121). It sums cusp.g2 on RealOps (elem.py kernels). The tail is handled at 279-284.
(b) run_d3 (297-322) sums d3.box over d3.boxes() (d3.py 183-219). Each box is either crude (222-236) or Gauss-Legendre with three error terms: _v_rules (125-142), and _outer_rule (165-180) in each of the s and t directions, the latter calling _int_v_bound (145-162). The total adds d3.tail_t (240-264) and tail_s_bound (267-276), all scaled by 64 (316).
(c) consts.py: the prefactors P2 and P3, c1_d1, c_ref, K_p and Gamma via lngamma (24-40), all through elem.exp_iv/log_iv.
(d) side24.transfer (side24.py 137-151), exact Fractions, giving eta. derived() (356-392) then forms c1*[1-eta, 1+eta] (369-370), c1/c_ref, I_cand and c_(d,24) (373).
Not on the claim path: controls.py (never imported by certificate.py); ia.Phi/Q_point/_mills (ia.py 204-279, imported nowhere); assembly_check, float_int_g2, float_T3 and the _*_float references in certificate.py (floating guards that can only raise).
audit.basic_operations:
Sound in ia.py.
- add, sub, mul and div (ia.py 36-57) apply one IEEE operation per corner product and then widen with dn/up (math.nextafter, 14-19), lower endpoint down and upper up. One-ulp widening also covers a faithful (not just correct) rounding and the subnormal range.
- div raises when the divisor interval contains 0 (54-55); cdiv raises if the lower bound of |b|^2 is <= 0 (cx.py 55-60).
- isqrt raises on a negative lower endpoint, uses math.sqrt (IEEE correctly rounded) and widens (110-115).
- sqr and pw handle sign cases (72-99). divc and scal take exact float constants (60-69).
- There is no math.fsum, math.prod, numpy or fused operation anywhere on the claim path. In Python, chained expressions such as c - z*p are separate binary64 operations.
- Exact power-of-two scalings: ldexp in exp_neg (191; results stay normal, since y <= 700 gives n <= 1009), frexp in log_pt (60).
- Large ints become floats only via Fraction.__float__ (correctly rounded int/int division), which from_frac then brackets exactly (27-33).

Exceptions:
1. Error-bound arithmetic is plain round-to-nearest float with relative slack, not interval operations:
   - gauss.error_bound (126-127) uses rho**(-2n) and rho**-2 (libm pow), then 1e-12 slack;
   - d3.box sums err_v with a plain sum() (208), then 1e-12 slack (209);
   - elem tails use m**k and math.factorial with a factor 2 (52, 101, 150-151, 247, 294);
   - the d = 2 tail uses U**7 and U**-14 (certificate.py 281-282); the t-tail uses T**7 and T**9 (d3.py 262-263).
   Each slack is ample for any libm with error < 1e3 ulp, but this trusts libm pow, contrary to NOTE.md 264.
2. scal(0.1, ...) at d3.py 256 breaks the exact-c precondition (ia.py 61). It is still sound: 0.1f = (1/10)(1+2^-54), and an error of z*2^-54 < ulp(z)/2 is absorbed by dn after correct rounding.
3. A NaN is silently dropped by Python min/max in ia.mul (49-50) and by the running max of bounds (d3.py 94, 139, 174, 176; certificate.py 245). It needs an infinity first. I found no route to overflow by reading:
   - exp raises above 700 (elem.py 30-31);
   - sin/cos raise above 1e6;
   - wmin*wmin and tmin*tmin cannot underflow, because slab endpoints are either 0, which raises, or at least about 1e-17.
   The packet records this limit itself (C54-A-FINITE-02).
audit.elementary_functions:
All are enclosed, with correct a priori bounds applied outward; libm values are never used as results.
- exp(-y) (ia.py 163-201): reduction y = n ln2 + r with r enclosed and checked in [-1e-9, 0.75]; degree-18 Taylor-Horner. Horner plus coefficient error is gamma_36 + gamma_18, about 54u, against the 56u used; truncation 0.75^19/19! = 3.5e-20 < 1e-19; the factor e^0.75 = 2.117 is covered by 2.12. y > 700 maps to [0, 2^-1000], which is valid since 700 > 1000 ln 2.
- exp(t) for t > 0 is 1/exp(-t) (elem.py 26-32).
- log (56-67): m in [1/sqrt2, sqrt2), 2 atanh((m-1)/(m+1)) with |u| <= 0.172, plus e*ln2. log1p (74-82): 2 atanh(t/(2+t)) with |u| <= 1/3. The atanh tail m^55/(55(1-m^2)) is correct, and doubled.
- atan (105-124): pi/2 - atan(1/t), then two halvings down to 0.199 < 0.21; alternating-series remainder bounded by the next term, doubled.
- sin/cos (132-171): k = round(t/(pi/2)), with r = t - k*HALF_PI enclosed and checked |r| <= 0.8; next-term remainders r^27/27! and r^26/26!, doubled; correct quadrant map.
- sin_iv/cos_iv (178-216) add +-1 at every critical point whose pi-enclosure meets the interval.
- Kernels (237-308) use the stated monotonicity, all true: E1 increasing; L decreasing on (-1, oo); A even and decreasing in |x|; Sinc decreasing on [0, 3] subset [0, pi]. Series tails: E1 2|t|^19/20!; Sinc 2|t|^22/23!. The Sinc range for |x| > 3 containing 0 uses the uncertified but true constant -0.2173 < min sinc = -0.217234 (308).
- Complex boxes (cx.py): the integral-hull forms of E1, L, A and Sinc, the closed forms (principal Log for Re(1+z) > 0.5; A for Re z > 0), the polar form of cpow for Re > 0, and ccos/csin/cexp are all valid enclosures. Each raises where its analyticity premise could fail.
- Direct bounds (cusp.py 122-189): branch cuts excluded by _off_cut, and |z^a| = |z|^a.
- Lemma A (identity theorem across overlapping slabs) and Lemma Q (|a_k| <= 2 M rho^-k, the bound 4M(1 + 1/(4n^2-1)) rho^-2n/(1 - rho^-2)) are correct.
- ellipse_slabs covers the closed ellipse; the 1e-12 inflations dominate the float errors in c, h and the slab endpoints.
- Gamma (consts.py 24-40): Stirling at y = q+10 with K = 10 and B_2..B_22 correct; remainder |B_22|/(22*21*y^21) (first omitted term, valid for real y > 0), exact Fractions, exact product prod (q+j).
- Tails checked against NOTE.md:
  - d = 2: |Re H| <= (36/19)^(5/8) u^-7 = 1.491 u^-7 < 1.5 u^-7 (certificate.py 279-284);
  - t > 15: |Phi| <= t^-2, so W(T^-7/7 +- T^-9/9), with int s^20 e^(-s^8 E) ds = Gamma(21/8)/(8 E^(21/8)) exact and E >= 3/16 clamped at 0.1874999 (d3.py 240-264);
  - s > 3: E[Y^2] <= a1^6/50 + 3a1^4 + 3a1^2, int Gt dt <= 2 s^16, s^36 <= e^(0.0875 s^8), total < 3.4e-289 < 1e-280 (267-276).
audit.constants_and_conversions:
All are enclosures.
- pi: Machin series with an exact Fraction remainder (ia.py 123-137).
- ln 2: sum 1/(j 2^j) with the tail 2/(J 2^J) (150-160).
- Every rational constant in the integrands goes through from_frac(Fr(q)), the tightest outward float pair (cusp.py 28-34, consts.py 59-60).
- Literal inputs 2.0, 3.0, 5.0, 6.0, 12.0, 30.0 are exact. sqrt(2 - sqrt2)/2, Gamma, rpow and the prefactors are interval-computed (consts.py 47-115).
- Gauss-Legendre nodes: exact rational Newton steps, then a strict sign change of P_n at r +- 2^-150, a disjointness check and a positivity check (gauss.py 68-112). Weights: exact midpoint value plus a Lipschitz term built from the valid bounds |P'_(n-1)| <= n(n-1)/2 and m = min|P| - D1 width (41-56). The math.cos seed is only a starting point.
- Lemma S: E, eps and eta are exact Fractions (side24.py 114-151). [1-eta, 1+eta] is rounded outward with from_frac (certificate.py 369).
- c_(d,24): the decimal strings become exact Fractions, then outward floats (373). The transcription check against ENCLOSURE.json is silently skipped when that file is absent (side24.py 217-218); this is provenance, not arithmetic.
- The one inexact literal used as an interval scale, 0.1 (d3.py 256), is sound (see basic_operations).
- Publication: Decimal(float) is exact; quantize is called with explicit ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING after a 1e-12 relative widening plus dn/up (certificate.py 341-353). There is no reliance on the default decimal context beyond 28-digit precision, which exceeds the 17 digits needed.
- The NOTE.md/README tables lie outside RESULTS.json in every row I compared.
audit.decisions:
Certification decisions use exact comparisons with the correct endpoints.
- compare() requires published_lo <= raw_lo and raw_hi <= published_hi, as exact Decimals with no tolerance (certificate.py 430-432). The 3e-12 slack (433-436) only rejects publications that are too loose.
- Lemma S premises are exact (side24.py 125-129, 141-149). The Gauss sign change uses a strict < 0 (gauss.py 90). The weight denominator guard is m <= 0, which raises (50).
- Choosing n, rho, crude versus Gauss-Legendre, and the representation (certificate.py 251-256; d3.py 104-122, 187) only selects which valid enclosure is used, and the chosen error bound is always added (269, 210).
- Exceptions are caught only as d3.FAIL, which rejects a representation or a rho (certificate.py 246; d3.py 96, 157, 178, 234) and never turns a failure into a pass.
- assembly_check and selftest are floating guards with tolerances; they can only abort.
- There are no asserts, so -O is harmless. Python specifics: CPython binary64 in round-to-nearest; separate operations, no contraction; nextafter; no numpy; no x87 dependence (one-ulp widening tolerates faithful rounding; only the scal(0.1) argument needs correct rounding, which SSE2 provides).
- Exception: the coverage of d3._sub is not decided anywhere in code (finding 1).

findings.issue:
Whether the d = 3 error bound is covered depends on run-time float bits that cannot be checked by reading.
- _sub(a, b, 2) ends at fl(a + fl(b - a)), not at b. When a < b/2, and with a in [2^-6, 2^-5) and b, b - a in [2^-5, 2^-4), writing a = A*2^-58 and b = B*2^-57, the endpoint is b - 2^-57 exactly when B is odd and A = 1 mod 4. In that case the v-sliver (b - 2^-57, b) is left out of the bound on the integral of |f3| dv (line 161).
- v_edges(tb) keeps 0.3/tb and 0.7/tb, and drops 0.5/tb, for 10 < tb <= 15. Both values fall in those binades for about 11.2 < tb <= 12.8.
- _int_v_bound calls v_edges with tb = the upper real abscissa of each t-ellipse slab (149) from _outer_rule('t') (176). For t-panels (8,11) and (11,15), several slab abscissae fall in that window. For example rho = 1.2, T = (11,15), slab j = 2 gives tb ~ 12.4917, which matches NOTE.md's own example (0.024016010673783495, 0.056037358238828154) to about 10 digits, as far as I can compute by hand.
- If the bit condition holds on a reached call, the M at line 176, and with it the Lemma Q term et (194, 209), is not proven. The 1e-12 slack almost certainly absorbs a 2^-57 sliver, but nothing in the code bounds |f3| on that sliver.
- NOTE.md 367-369 says the published run never reaches such a case, citing an external audit of actual calls. That depends on which rho values _search reaches at run time and on the low bits of the slab abscissae, so it cannot be verified without running the code.
- Only d = 3 is affected (T3, c1^(3), I_cand d=3, the d = 3 ratios, and [P] d=3). d = 1 and d = 2 never call _sub. The S/T calls of _sub are exact on the published grids: either Sterbenz applies or a = 0, and b - a lies below b's binade. Their halves only need to cover interior nodes.
- Fix: make _sub return b as its last endpoint, or raise when it does not.

libm pow (float ** int) is trusted in error-bound arithmetic, protected only by relative slack: 1e-12 in error_bound for rho**(-2n) and rho**-2, a factor 2 in the series tails, and 1.5 versus 1.491 plus 1e-12 in the tails, which also assume 15.0**7 and 15.0**9 are exact. Any libm within about 1e3 ulp is safe, but this cannot be verified by reading, and it contradicts NOTE.md 264 ('No libm transcendental is trusted'). Fix: compute these with exact Fractions.

NaN is silently dropped: ia.mul takes min/max over corner products that may include NaN (0*inf), and the running max of bounds discards a NaN (m starts at 0.0). An infinite intermediate would therefore shrink M without any error. By reading I found no route to overflow: exp raises above 700, sin/cos raise above 1e6, magnitudes stay bounded, and wmin*wmin and tmin*tmin cannot underflow on these grids. The packet records this limit (C54-A-FINITE-02, NOTE.md 370-371) but has no finite-result guard.

err_v is a plain float sum() of positive terms; its relative error of about 10u is covered by the (1 + 1e-12) factor. NOTE.md 267 ('Every sum is an interval sum') is not literally true for the error-bound sums.

scal(0.1, X) breaks scal's exact-constant precondition. It is still sound, because 0.1f = (1/10)(1 + 2^-54) and z*2^-54 < ulp(z)/2, so dn(fl(0.1f X_lo)) <= X_lo/10 under correct rounding. This should be documented, or replaced with from_frac(Fr(1, 10)).
Sinc_iv returns (-0.2173, 1.0) for |x| > 3 intervals containing 0, using a stated rather than code-certified constant. It is true: min sin(x)/x = cos(4.4934) = -0.217234 > -0.2173.

enclosure_check returns None, so the check is skipped silently, when coefficients/side24_v1/ENCLOSURE.json is not reachable. This affects only the provenance of the consumed c_(d,24), not the interval arithmetic.

audit.summary:
The verdict is INDETERMINATE, and only the d = 3 results depend on the unresolved point. Apart from that, the code is justified binary64 interval reasoning.
- Every basic operation on the claim path is one IEEE operation followed by one-ulp outward widening, with zero-divisor and negative-sqrt guards.
- pi, ln 2, the Gauss-Legendre nodes and weights, Gamma, Lemma S and all rational constants are exact rationals or outward enclosures.
- exp, log, log1p, atan, sin/cos and the four kernels have correct range reductions and correct, doubled remainder bounds. I re-derived Lemma Q, Lemma A, the complex-box forms and the three tails against NOTE.md.
- Publication and --check use exact outward Decimal containment with no tolerance.

The blocking point is d3._sub (d3.py 40-41): it can drop a 2^-57 sliver at the top of a v-panel. My reading puts the triggering pair (0.3/tb, 0.7/tb) on the published path, through t-slab abscissae near 11.2 to 12.8 in _int_v_bound (d3.py 145-162, 176). Whether a loss actually happens depends on run-time bits, and the packet relies on an external actual-call audit (NOTE.md 367-369) that cannot be checked without running the code.

Two minor points: error bounds trust libm pow with only relative slack, contrary to NOTE.md 264, and Python min/max would silently drop a NaN bound (no route to one found by reading).

Two one-line changes would make this SOUND_AS_INTERVAL_REASONING: have _sub end exactly at b, and compute the error-bound powers in exact Fractions. Alternatively, a reviewed replay could confirm that no reached _sub call loses its endpoint. This record advises the A3 field only; it certifies nothing.

disputed_points.point: The BLOCKING finding is real, and NOTE.md's own example is exactly this claim-path call. I would describe it as an uncertified step, not a demonstrated enclosure failure; that is why the verdict is INDETERMINATE rather than UNSOUND.
disputed_points.evidence: Mechanism: d3.py 41 returns last endpoint fl(a + fl(b - a)). With a in [2^-6, 2^-5) and b, b - a in [2^-5, 2^-4), ties-to-even give b - 2^-57 exactly when B is odd and A = 1 mod 4 (I checked both rounding steps). The window: v_edges drops 0.5/tb and keeps (0.3/tb, 0.7/tb) for 11.2 < tb <= 12.8. For rho = 1.2, T = (11, 15), slab j=2, gauss.py 136-142 gives x1 = 13 - ax/4 with ax = 2.0333333333353667. So 0.3/x1 = (36/1499)(1 + 4.07e-14) = 0.0240160106737835 and 0.7/x1 = 0.0560373582388282, which match NOTE.md 367-368 to within one ulp. Size: the lost sliver can move M only by about 2^-57 sup|f3|. Against the (1+1e-12) slacks (gauss.py 127, d3.py 209), the enclosure would fail only if |f3| on the sliver were about 4000 times the bound on the adjacent sub-interval. Nothing in the code excludes that, but it is not plausible for an analytic integrand.

disputed_points.point: Reachability is stronger than the audit says, and it does not depend on rho = 1.2. Triggering pairs are evaluated on the published path, which makes NOTE.md's external actual-call audit load-bearing.
disputed_points.evidence: TOL3 = 1e-11 (certificate.py 38), so crude needs <= 1e-12 (d3.py 187). The main boxes with T = (8, 11) or (11, 15) carry about 1e-10 to 1e-9, so they go to _outer_rule('t') at d3.py 194. _search (d3.py 108) always tries rho = 3.0 first. Its slab upper abscissae are about 11.333 and 12.167 for T = (11, 15) (j = 1, 2) and about 11.375 and 12.0 for T = (8, 11) (j = 6, 7). All four lie in (11.2, 12.8] and reach v_edges at d3.py 149 unless an earlier slab raises. Whether their fl(0.3/tb) and fl(0.7/tb) bits trigger the loss cannot be determined by reading, and RESULTS.json does not record rho_t per box.

disputed_points.point: Addition: the sliver also leaves the t-analyticity premise uncertified, not just the bound's magnitude.
disputed_points.evidence: _int_v_bound (d3.py 151-161) is also the only place that checks analyticity of f3(s, v, .) on the t-slab for each v. That check is needed for Lemma Q applied to I_V f in t. For v in (vb - 2^-57, vb) no box is evaluated. The remedy is the same: make _sub end exactly at b, or raise.

disputed_points.point: Partial correction to the MINOR libm-pow finding. The elem.py series tails are not load-bearing; only the Gauss error bound and the tail formulas depend on pow.
disputed_points.evidence: Tails such as E1 2|t|^19/20! (about 1.6e-24 at |t| = 0.5), Sinc (about 2e-29), sin/cos (<= 0.8^27/27!, about 2e-31) and atanh/atan (< 1e-22) all lie far below the one-ulp widening of the partial sums in _with_err (elem.py 20-22). The pow dependence is real only at gauss.py 126-127 (rho**(-2n), 1e-12 slack), certificate.py 281-282 (U**-14, and U**7 assumed exact) and d3.py 262-263 (T**7, T**9).

cross.reasoning:
I re-read d3.py, gauss.py, cusp.py, cx.py, elem.py, ia.py, consts.py, side24.py (transfer), the certificate.py drivers and publication, and NOTE.md 240-375. I ran no code.

The rest of the path is justified interval reasoning, which supports the audit:
- Gauss-Legendre nodes come from an exact sign change at r +- 2^-150, and the weights use a valid Lipschitz enclosure (|P'_(n-1)| <= n(n-1)/2) (gauss.py 41-112).
- I re-derived the Lemma Q bound from the even-k sum, and the slabs cover the closed ellipse with 1e-12 inflation (gauss.py 124-146).
- cx.py: the complex box forms are valid (the integral hulls of E1, L, A and Sinc, principal Log for Re > 0, the polar cpow).
- cusp.py: the direct-form bounds are valid (|z^a| = |z|^a, _off_cut, H* = conj H(conj w)).
- The safe-form identity holds: 1 - Re Phi = -R E1(R) + e^R (I^2/2) Sinc(I/2)^2.
- Tails: (36/19)^(5/8) = 1.491 < 1.5, |Phi| <= t^-2, the exact s-integral Gamma(21/8)/(8 E^(21/8)), the 0.1874999 < 3/16 clamp, and the s > 3 bound of about 3.5e-289 < 1e-280.
- scal(0.1, X) at d3.py 256 is sound under correct rounding.
- Exact Decimal containment in compare() (certificate.py 430-432).

The _sub calls on S and T are exact. The only non-Sterbenz S pair, (2.8/tb, 0.6), has b - a below b's binade, so its rounding error is less than ulp(b)/2.

The one unresolved dependence is d3._sub at d3.py 40-41, used at 151 and 161. A 2^-57 sliver at the top of a (0.3/tb, 0.7/tb) v-panel can be left uncovered, and the published d = 3 results (T3, c1^(3), the d = 3 ratios and the [P] d = 3 rows) rest on run-time float bits and on an external actual-call audit (NOTE.md 367-369) that cannot be checked by reading.

The gap is real in the reasoning, and the rho = 3.0 calls make it likely to be exercised on the published path. A failure of the final enclosure is not demonstrated, so the verdict is INDETERMINATE, not UNSOUND. d = 1 and d = 2 are unaffected. Two changes would make the record SOUND_AS_INTERVAL_REASONING: make _sub return b as its last endpoint (or raise), and compute the error-bound powers in exact Fractions.
